corrections.what_happened: The row's retrieval held the first call (claude-sonnet-5) and the embedder's requests added into one sum: a language model's tokens and the embedder's tokens were one number, and attempts counted the first call's tries while calls counted both; in the two questions whose first call was refused and asked again, its time_s left out the refused call's seconds, which only its retry_s held. search_time_s held the embedder's seconds, which were also in retrieval.time_s, and, in those two questions, the refused call's seconds. build_stats held the seconds of the run's start, not what building the graph cost, which stood only in index.build_cost. The graph block named the database only: the checkout the run was made from had no build record of the graph, and nothing counted the graph. The sha256 of the code files and of the build cost file were of the files with the Windows line ends the checkout wrote, so none matched the commit's.

rule.text:
1. A row's retrieval is its own call records summed per model (harness.capture.usage_by_model),
     the answer call left out. The answer call is the record whose system text is the harness's
     answer instruction; it is marked role: answer, and its tokens must be the generator's.
  2. The entries must hold what the row recorded: the same calls, tokens in, tokens out and cached
     tokens in all.
  3. artefact_v4 only: search_time_s loses the embedder's seconds (lock_wait_s + encode_s of the
     row's embed records) and the seconds of the first-call tries that did not answer (the chat
     entry's retry_s).
  4. build_stats gets one entry per model, from the run's own manifest: lucene none; vector the
     embedder, from its build_stats and the stored file's cost note; artefact_v4 from
     index.build_cost (artefact_v4.build_stats_from_cost).
  5. artefact_v4 only: the graph block takes the graph's last build record and the graph counted
     now (orchestrator.graph_census), after a check that the graph holds now what the run counted
     at its start.
  6. artefact_v4 only: the sha256 of the code files (meta.provenance.source_sha256) and of the
     build cost file (index.build_cost_file_sha256) become those of the commit's files, their
     line ends as git holds them (LF), after a check that each recorded value is the commit's
     file with the Windows line ends the checkout wrote.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: No answer, context, id, score or judge call is changed; the call records are changed only by the answer call's role.

A retrieval entry's seconds are the tries' and the embedder's own seconds from the call records. The sum the arm recorded held the seconds around each call, so the entries hold a little less; that rest is the arm's own work, in timing.wall_s.
timing.wall_s and the stamps are unchanged.

The graph census counts and reads no value. That the graph counted now is the graph the run read rests on the check named in checks: the counts and the facet layer's hashes the run recorded at its start are those of now.
The graph's last build record is from before the October steps of index.build_cost; its version and census hash describe the graph as that build left it.

corrections.what_happened: The two id-based scores were calculated on the row's context_ids, which hold only the records of the texts handed over whole. The artefact's text is a chunk of one or more records, so the records of the cut chunk whose text the answer model got whole were not counted.

rule.text:
1. A record counts as retrieved when the answer model got its text whole. The harness's cut
     (char_budget.cut_at_budget) hands over the start of the text that crosses the limit, and the
     row's context_ids hold only the records of the texts handed over whole.
  2. artefact_v4 only: a chunk's text is its records as JSON, one a line, in the order of its ids
     (artefact_v4._hand_over, artefact_v2._resolve_chunk). In the cut chunk, every line that ends
     before the cut is a record the answer model got whole; a chunk that is part of one record's
     text has none.
  3. context_recall_id and context_precision_id are calculated again by RAGAS's own
     IDBasedContextRecall and IDBasedContextPrecision on the row's context_ids with those records
     added, against the questions file's citations; every other score and every other file stays
     as it is.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: No answer, context, context_ids, other score or judge call is changed; arm_outputs.jsonl is as it was. Lucene and vector are not changed: their cut text is one record, and the answer model got only its start.

checks.what: RAGAS on the row's context_ids gives the stored score again
each cut chunk's lines are its records in the order of its ids
